mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary policy, which lowers discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 0.25% signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle, which increases discount rates and compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in high FEDFUNDS periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous month-over-month increase in CPIAUCSL above 0.5% and decline in UNRATE below -0.1% signals an overheating economy, prompting aggressive monetary tightening by the Fed, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in triggered instances are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, a simultaneous month-over-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) signals an impending economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in late-cycle expansion with both HOUST and RSAFS declining are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).
